resources.string: Tishina records ambient sound pressure using your phone\'s microphone. Save measurements, review history and share the readings — fully offline, with no third-party analytics.

Tishina is not a certified sound-level meter and is not a replacement for a Class 1 or Class 2 instrument under IEC 61672. Smartphone MEMS microphones vary between devices and even between units of the same model — typical accuracy after calibration is ±3 to ±5 dB(A) in the 50–95 dB range, with larger errors near the limits of the microphone's dynamic range and below ambient room noise.

For occupational or regulatory measurements, follow the relevant standard with calibrated equipment. The NIOSH Sound Level Meter App study (Kardous & Shaw, 2014, doi:10.1121/1.4865269) showed that smartphone-based meters can approach professional accuracy only after careful calibration against a reference instrument.

Use Tishina as a quick, indicative tool: room loudness, traffic noise around a window, whether a neighbour's music is closer to 50 dB or 90 dB. It is suitable for raising awareness and for personal recordings, not for evidence in legal or workplace-safety contexts.
